_note: Answer key for the scan-guard corpus test. Committed because it is the judgement;
tests/fixtures/bash-commands.jsonl is regenerable machine-local data and is git-ignored.
id = sha256(command)[0:16] as written by scripts/export-bash-corpus.mjs.
A label records ONE fact, decided by hand against the raw session record: this command
walks `/` or all of `$HOME`. It deliberately does not record the guard's verdict — whether
a walk is worth blocking is policy and lives in the classifier. Two commands labelled here
are 75 ms of work (`find ~ -maxdepth 1`-shaped) and one 5,550 s command is bounded at 4,
which is exactly the tension the README has to state.
Scored by hand, not by the classifier, because the first automated pass at scoring the four
`find /` calls got two of four wrong (a trailing `echo "(search done)"` reads as an empty
result to a classifier that stops early).
Not labelled, and deliberately so: `bash -c "find /"` and any scan inside a quoted string,
a script file, `xargs`, or `python -c 'os.walk(...)'`. Those are documented escapes of a
quote-aware detector and are pinned as limits in the unit tests, not as recall targets here.
dur = wall time of the bash call from the session log. The two 5,550 s rows finished in one
turn and share the wait, so they are 92 minutes of wall time, not 184.
2026-10-30: 29 labelled commands over 13,084 bash calls. The handoff's 19 counted only the
`find /` and `find ~` spellings; these add the ones bounded at depth 3-5, the two at cwd
(`cd ~ && find .`), the `fd` spelling, and the four benchmark commands the audit itself ran. No command was reclassified.

Cross-check against `knowledge/broad-fs-scans.md`: the four `find /` calls it scored by hand are all here — 0.8 s (cb6d54e), 24.5 s (7ac127), 839 s aborted (69c7ce), 179 s found it (7f29ff). 19 and 29 are one habit counted by lookups with different reach.

broad.2fed60b34537ab5e: 5,550 s, the worst call in the corpus: `find ~ -maxdepth 4 -name knowledge -type d` twice in one command, the second inside `$( … )`. Bounded at 4 — the guard's depth predicate lets it through, which is why the bounded tier warns instead of staying silent.
broad.8620034767f5bcc6: 5,550 s (same turn as the row above): `find ~ -maxdepth 3 -iname '*second-brain*'` after two `ls ~/Projects`.
broad.03348903971de996: 1,716 s: `find /Users/<user> -name dailyContext.md`, unbounded, hunting for the memory bank.
broad.69c7ce2e1a1ff7fd: 839 s, isError, "Command aborted": `find / -name "three.module*.js"`. Nothing was recovered afterwards. One of the four `find /` calls.
broad.498ed237192b3b06: 243 s: `find ~ -name "*0.9e*"`, unbounded, hunting a lost file.
broad.b7fd5a95f276a32d: 181 s: `find ~ -maxdepth 5 \( -name rehearse-integrations.ts … \)`, in a long recovery command.
broad.7f29ff71bfcae00b: 179 s: `find / -name 'jogoforca-port.md'` — the one `find /` that paid off. It found a file pi had echoed back as a relative path.
broad.6b19d3de591f5df0: 50 s: `timeout 150 find ~` unbounded, then `fd -H . ~/Projects`. Run by the audit that sized this guard, 2026-10-29.
broad.7ac127ee6faef574: 25 s: `find / -maxdepth 8 -type d -name pi-vcc`. Added nothing — `ls -d` globs earlier in the same command had already answered. One of the four `find /` calls.
broad.ccee62c97b5f1d4c: 15 s: `timeout 20 find ~ -maxdepth 4 -name knowledge -type d`, the Spotlight-vs-find comparison run by the audit.
broad.27f1dc8402232487: 11 s, isError: `find /Users/<user> -maxdepth 4 -name tmux-powerlinerc` and `-maxdepth 3 -type d -name tmux-powerline` in one command.
broad.9e4b26468d16ca17: 7 s: `find ~ -maxdepth 5 -name bin -path '*/bin/rails'` — looking for a Rails project that was never on this machine.
broad.d8b448236be803e5: 5 s: the depth benchmark — `find ~ -maxdepth $d` for d in 1..4, `find / -maxdepth 3`, `fd -H . ~`. Depth from a loop variable: unknown to the guard, so not bounded. Run by the audit.
broad.83a79b193d488e40: 1.4 s: `which agenmux || find /Users/<user> -name 'agenmux*' -type f`, unbounded fallback.
broad.cb6d54e3c8ff7752: 0.8 s: `find / -maxdepth 4 -name probe.mjs -path '*tools*'` — found nothing, and `find /` at depth 4 is the cheap end of walking the volume. One of the four `find /` calls.
broad.3f0efa48ba6d3bbe: 0.3 s: `find ~ -maxdepth $d -name zzz-no-such-file` for d in 1..3, the timing harness. Depth from a variable → unknown → not bounded.
broad.dfb862ce2788069c: 0.0 s, isError: `find ~ -d '/Projects/AI/test1/' -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d` — a mistaken predicate on a real home root. Labelled because the walk would have started at `$HOME`.
broad.61553a7151b799c4: 2.2 s: `cd ~ && … find . -maxdepth 2 -iname '*homelab*'`. Root is `.`; only the `cd ~` in the same command makes it a home walk.
broad.6fcced738dd1b585: 7.0 s: `fd -H 'jogoforca-port\.md' ~`, the whole-home half of a two-line benchmark — the classifier found this one and the loose candidate net in the export script did not, because for `fd` the first operand is the pattern and the root is the second.
broad.4cfa32f87199ba91: 0.5 s: `cd ~ && … timeout 60 find . -maxdepth 4 -iname '*powerline*'`. Session cwd was `~/.terminal`, so the root comes from the `cd`, not from context.
